This is going to be a huge problem in the future, plastics, electronics and other temperature sensitive outdoor products will degrade or stop working and retailers should make operating temperatures a basic factor in choosing products to sell to consumers. In 2024 Phoenix, Arizona had 64 days when temperatures were 110 or above. Saturday arrived and still no change in shipping status to indicate the item was shipped--in fact, the only update was to state I was receiving a refund--so I called Amazon again. I had the call escalated and I was told the item was never replaced and that none of the agents should have told me what they did. It was also too late to order that item as new orders would arrive after the surgery date. I looked for a different clear protein drink (that isn't red or purple). By now the surgery was only a few days away. The item I found indicated it could be delivered same day, between 5 and 10 p.m. Eureka, I thought. I ordered it. Of course it didn't arrive. That night the app updated to say that it would be delivered by 8 a.m. the next day. It wasn't. I called Amazon again. This time they have no idea why the item wasn't delivered and they still had no idea if or when the item might be delivered today. I had the call escalated. She didn't know either. She also couldn't reach the area that handles shipping to find out when the item would be shipped. She ended up refunding the first item (while not canceling it) and recommending a new order be put in to try to get the item delivered by this afternoon--halfway through the clear liquids day. I did as she suggested and put the second order it, but I really have very little confidence  Amazon can make it happen anymore. Unfortunately, these are not the only examples of failed and late deliveries with this company. It's become commonplace. While I was on the phone with the escalation team, I submitted my order for the first items I am moving to Walmart and away from Amazon. I will find replacements for the rest of my items and then cancel Prime before the end of the month. For those who may be holding off on canceling Prime because you like the streaming, be aware that after you cancel you can pay for a streaming-only option for $9 a month--less than the $15 a month or so we pay for Prime shipping. Review Title: Appalling Customer Service When dealing Security
Review Text: Appalling Customer Service When dealing with the Security of Your Property I was an Amazon Prime customer for 5 years, and after 4 months of couriers ignoring delivery instructions, asked Amazon to take action on drivers that refuse to to do so, as it was causing a security problem.It's important to note we have elderly parents at home that need a little extra time to respond to a courier. We also live a in time where security issues arise from time to time, particularly in urban areas.Theft can be a problem at any time but when deliveries are left unattended for any length of time, it's a red wragg to a bull! I get that drivers are generally in a rush to get to the next delivery and are human, but these days there's a  noticeable trend for couriers to often ignore instructions to wait until someone answers the door,drop the item on the doorstep and move on. One customer support person informed me that these are called "unattended deliveries" Genius.Reporting this to their Deliveries and Logistics department turned out to be a fruitless exercise (so please save yourself the time and hope). Despite assurances to look into the problem, the problem kept reoccurring, and bizarrely logistics kept on giving the same assurances. Its eternal loop!They may well investigate the problem, whilst it continues to happen but will claim, due to GDPR and to protect the drivers identity claimants are not allowed to know the outcome of the investigation in any way. Utter garbage.So you will never know if the problem has even been addressed and since it keeps happening, whatever efforts they may or may not of made, ultimately amount to nothing. I'm sure you can spot the loophole here..I'm sure they are lovely people doing their best, but I have cancelled my prime membership and saved 9 pounds a month for a similar service - they will not offer any other resolution and, as a manager told me after 3 hours of speaking to customer support,  "we cannot change our policy and there's nothing more we can do" Avoid this happening to you because they are not serious about your security.

Review Title: Amazon was great, but not a great value anymore
Review Text: I started using Amazon back in the 1990s as a graduate student. I purchased my textbooks there as it was cheaper than the university bookstore and tax free. Fast forward to 2008 when Amazon asked me to try prime for free. I did. And didn't realize they charged me $79 for the membership. I decided to keep it because products were cheaper than at on-ground stores, no taxes and free shipping. Then in 2012 China clamped down on counterfeit producers and stopped them from selling product in China. In 2012 Amazon opened the door to these Chinese sellers and Amazon became flooded with a bunch of junk products. The price of prime kept rising, but I kept it because of Prime video and 2-day delivery. When I became sick I relied on Amazon more. Now Amazon is expensive. They have moved lots of shows to Freevee, which I don't watch because I don't do ad TV. And to add insult to injury this year, 2024, they started adding ads to Prime Video and demanding an extra $3/month to remove the ads, citing all of the other services they added to Prime. I don't use those other services, so it is bloatware to me. Stuff isn't being delivered in 2 days anymore. And there have been times when products were lost in their shipping facilities and not delivered. You call Amazon and they outsource their customer service overseas, these people have no way to contact the drivers. This is rubbish. The seller ALWAYS has contact with shipping! Paying extra for same-day delivery doesn't guarantee it will be delivered same-day. Amazon stopped packing cushioning in boxes so I've received items damaged. I've received spoiled food items. I was horrified to learn the tea I was drinking expired months before. Once they shipped me pet food meant to be sold in Mexico. So, even though you purchase from one seller they ship the product that is closer to your domicile, which might not be the same quality. Prices aren't cheaper than the on-ground store anymore, sometimes it is higher. Taxes are included too. So there is no value to having Amazon anymore. I even submitted my SSN & 1099 to sell t-shirts on Amazon. They stopped adding people to the program that didn't have a huge social media following. But refused to delete my information from their database. Lastly, I purchased a product that was defective, a sports watch. I wanted to exchange it. The watch cost hundreds of dollars. The customer service rep wanted to offer me $25 for it. I demanded a supervisor and the US support team processed the exchange. When Hurricane Beryl was bearing down on Houston TX, I ordered the Midland NOAA radio bundle so I could be notified of tornados and floods should I lose power. My home was hit by a tornado in May 2024, so the threat was real. I paid extra for same day delivery. Amazon split the bundle with one part being delivered in a week and the other same-day, except they never delivered it and promised to deliver it AFTER the hurricane. I called and spoke to three reps. One had a fake barking dog sound and you couldn't hear a word she said. After 30 minutes she just told me to call the number I called to get her. Another promised to expedite it. He didn't. Finally I canceled the delivery with the third person. The product was sitting in Houston, I'm in Houston. I don't know why they refused to deliver it. I had to eventually purchase it from another company. This company that started out well is not the same as it was in the past when it cared about its customers. It doesn't care about its employees nor customers now, it only cares about profit. I will not be renewing my prime membership in October. And I will shop other online and on-ground retailers.

It can be hit or miss since things do get damaged in delivery, items can be defective, etc. I totally understand sometimes things happen.  Customers should not be penalized for these issues and customer service should be assisting instead of the unprofessional behavior and being hung up on intentionally. Review Title: Hands down THE best customer service…
Review Text: Hands down THE best customer service I've experienced online. I'm in Denmark and have been buying goods from the German Amazon for about a decade now.I've just been given my latest refund, which was for an awful Logitech MX Keys keyboard which luckily had one of its keys fall off after about 18 months, meaning I was still under warranty. I hoped to then be able to sell the brand-new replacement for a decent amount and buy a better keyboard, but Amazon just offered a full refund, which I happily accepted.I've had returns on close to ten orders, some of which have been swiftly closed with "refund issued, no need to return the item," the others returned with a prepaid parcel slip that just needs to be printed and stuck on the box, and once they've received the item back, a refund has been issued.Once I bought twelve bottles of baby oil (enough to get free shipping), and it was delivered damaged with three bottles having escaped through a hole. I called the local carrier and was put in queue as number 90-something. While waiting I checked the Amazon website and discovered the option to have Amazon call you up. I activated it and was immediately called on my phone by an employee who promptly refunded me money for the three missing bottles, no questions asked. The local carrier called me back two hours later.This last refund was set in motion by the friendliest German supporter who laughed with me at my broken German and did his best to follow my better English.If there's one negative, it's that the search function on their own website is basically useless, so I have to use Google with "site:amazon.de" added to the query instead.I see many negative reviews based on having been fooled by refund scammers, fake websites, or forgetting your password and blaming Amazon, hating on Bezos (which I agree with), or some other random own-fault issue.I've spent at least 10k € over a decade and NEVER had a bad experience with them.People, if someone randomly calls you up and say they're from Amazon (or any other business), hang up the phone and block that number.

Review Title: Truth about Amazon practices are not allowed in product reviews..
Review Text: Just like others, we traditionally have great experiences ordering from Amazon; however, when we wrote a review about their sales/shipping practices, Amazon refused to post it, citing "doesn't meet community guidelines." The only part of the review Amazon could be referring to, is that we indicated that Amazon permits sellers to charge shipping fees for a product that Amazon warehouses ship for free - let me clarify that. If the seller has product in stock, "they" ship it and charge a delivery fee. If they do not have it in stock, but Amazon has it in their warehouse, Amazon ships it directly, with no delivery fee added. Yeah, that sounds totally backwards, but that was the information we received from Amazon Customer Service. We stated in our review that this is not a "customer first" approach, because Amazon does not clearly notify the buyer about this practice. I guess Amazon does not like "truths" being posted within reviews on their own website. Amazon used to be the best "big business" company for customer service, but they have slowly and steadily become a "money first" entity. Need more proof? Enjoy the ads through Prime Video.

Review Title: How far the Mighty Amazon has Fallen
Review Text: I can't begin to describe how far Amazon has fallen over the years.  I was a customer from the beginning.  I was with Prime shortly after it came out.  I seriously thought it was the best company in the world, until it wasn't.  Then it wasn't even close.  Amazon now has among the worst customer service I encounter anywhere.  It rivals Comcast and Verizon Fios for the worst service you can even conceive of.  There's literally no way to describe the thousand ways Amazon fails at basic stuff.  It's service is a nightmare now.  You're sent off to a foreign country, with people who are supremely unhelpful, with the simplest issues taking hours to resolve.  I'm over it.  I no longer trust Amazon.  It's that simple.  Most recent case in point: I called Synchrony Bank, the issuer of the Amazon store card, to pay my bill.  It said the balance was over $400, so I thought I'd go through to a live person and see what the purchases were, to make sure nothing was unauthorized.  I recognized every purchase, except one.  There was an $11 charge for Amazon digital services.  I knew I hadn't authorized any digital purchases, so told them to put me through to Amazon.  The Indian man I spoke with was completely unhelpful.  Mind you, I mean him or anyone else no disrespect for being foreign.  He spoke with a thick accent likely because English was his second language.  GOOD FOR HIM.  It's something to be proud of.  But it also makes it very difficult to take care of issues that have any degree of complexity at all. He insisted I definitely ordered Amazon Music Unlimited, because I played [unintelligible] on my Alexa device.  What was the name of it?  "It was [unintelligible]"  HUH?  SAY THAT AGAIN SLOWLY?  Literally, his accent was so thick I couldn't tell at all what he was saying.  After repeating it a fourth time, I made out the word "noise."  It hit me that Amazon was charging me $11 a month to play "brown noise" on my bedroom Alexa device.  I've played that as a background sleep noise for YEARS.  Didn't start in December.  I've literally played it for about 3-5 years, every single night.  Suddenly it apparently started charging me for it in December.  I never heard it ask me ANYTHING about a subscription and certainly never agreed to any such thing.  But that didn't convince this Amazon rep, who apparently could read my mind and insisted I absolutely did order it.  I grew increasingly annoyed, especially as he kept going silent for 20, 30, 40 seconds at a time without saying a word, no hold or anything.. just silence.  Finally I told him, "why are you being silent?  I don't know what you're doing."  He then hung up on me.  So much for customer service.  I called angrier now and spoke with a second rep.  She was so very sorry the first rep hung up on me.  If I would just take more time out of my Saturday night to explain everything all over again and verify myself again... which I had no choice but to do.  She took a complaint on the last rep, but said she couldn't help me.  I'd have to be transferred to Amazon music.  Mind you, by this time it's nearly 1 am in the morning on a Sunday morning.  She puts me on hold... and I wait and I wait and wait some more.  About 15 minutes she comes back and says "I'm sorry for the long wait.  I'm still in the queue to speak with Amazon music."  I told her I would wait.  She puts me back on hold... 20 minutes pass... 30 minutes pass... 40 minutes pass.  Finally I had to give up.  She never came back on the line to say anything.  Just the same canned music playing over and over and over and over on a loop.  Called again.  Asked for a supervisor, but my phone died because I'd been held on the line so long.  He didn't call back.  I gave up because I had to give up.  Otherwise, I'd have a stroke from my anger and high blood pressure.  Amazon, you suck. Every single time I have a problem now, this is what I encounter.  Amazon is no longer a great company.  It's a company that will cut every corner, that disrespects its customers and their time, and that cares only about its bottom line.  It will go the way of Sears because it deserves to.

Review Title: I've been a pretty frequent amazon…
Review Text: I've been a pretty frequent amazon customer over at least the last two decades. The downfall started with a decision to purchase a macbook pro for around $3000. I greeted the amazon delivery person, I gave him the passcode several times- he kept repeating it back incorrectly. I took the package and remarked to my girlfriend that man they make macs light these days. I opened the package to find an obviously used and abused macbook box. I opened the box with an ever increasing heart rate as I knew at this point my worst fears were about to be realized. It was EMPTY! My girlfriend rushed out the door to the driver who was just down the street. He stated you want to look in the back of my truck? Nothing I can do, call amazon support. Of course I called right away. I sat on hold for at least 30-40 mins. Amazon's first attempt at resolving the issue was to tell me there was nothing that could be done since I gave them the OTP- they stated I should call the police???!!!! Little did I know the issues would only continue from here. Later that evening I received an email stating my account had most likely been hacked and all my orders were cancelled. Next I came to find out that any order around $100+ would require a OTP- meaning they send you a passcode via email a couple hrs before your order arrives that you're forced to give to the delivery person- meaning you have to be present all day long if you actually want to receive your order. That's exactly the opposite of what amazon was designed to be. I called in multiple times to have this obstruction / inconvenience removed. One person from logistics stated maybe I should buy my macbook from apple like he did? I asked if he ever bought anything on amazon for $100+ he stated no. After talking to several more people from all over the world one person agreed to give me a partial refund of around $79 of the $139 I was so exhausted I agreed to it. I now realize that it makes no sense, given it's only almost April 1st and a prorated refund would be $100+??? This has been a pretty ridiculous experience to say the least. Review Title: Amazon closed my account without an explanation
Review Text: A couple of weeks ago, Amazon abruptly canceled my account. I was attempting to access my account to make a purchase, and upon reaching the login page and entering my credentials, the following message appeared: ‘Your account has been terminated for improper use of Amazon services. We have sent you an email with more information.’ (It was written in Italian, I translated it with Google translate). However, no email arrived in my inbox despite repeated attempts. I began searching online to see if anyone else had encountered the same issue. I found an email address where I could file a complaint. They responded stating: ‘as already communicated to you, we have closed this account. From our records, we have previously terminated your account for violating the terms of our user agreement. Following termination of your account due to breach of contract, you are not permitted to open a new account or use another account to place orders on our site. Following a thorough evaluation, we have decided not to restore your full access to this account. It will therefore not be possible for you to place orders on our site. Any digital content purchased with this account is still available to you. To access the content, click the Manage content and devices link in the My Orders menu on Amazon.it.’ Despite my attempts to seek clarification, they provided the same generic responses, failing to explain the exact reason for the account termination and how I violated the terms of the agreement. Furthermore, they mentioned that I could still access digital content purchased with the account, which was untrue since my account was closed, leaving me without access to anything.Adding insult to injury, I own a Kindle that was linked to my account. A few days later, I attempted to read a book on my Kindle. As I am Russian and my Amazon account is Italian (and all the books in the Amazon store are either in Italian or English), I purchase eBooks from Russian websites and download them via USB from my PC to my Kindle. However, that night when I opened my Kindle, it was EMPTY!!! All my books were gone! And on the screen was the login page to the Amazon account, which I no longer had access to. Here arises an interesting question: how did they learn that my account was closed if my device was not connected to Wi-Fi? This implies that Amazon has another means of controlling my data and my device. All the books I downloaded, all the notes I made in the books, all the progress I made (I usually read several books at the same time) - everything was gone! An empty Kindle!!!I am deeply disappointed and angry with the situation and feel utterly helpless in resolving this problem. My account was canceled without explanation, I cannot ask questions through the app's customer service as my account is closed, Amazon support has ceased responding to my emails, my Kindle books have been deleted, and there is no one who seems to care or can offer assistance in any way to address this issue.

Review Title: They're so bad it's hard to know where to start
Review Text: It's hard to know where to start because there is now so much wrong with this company's services.Having been an Amazon Prime customer for well over a decade I have seen a lot of changes but recently the service has gone downhill to the point that I will not be renewing my subscription when it next expires.Particular issues that I've experiences are:1. Fake products - There are now a large number of cheap/dangerous knockoff products on amazon and it is impossible to tell from the listings which are genuine and which are the fakes.2. Reviews - The review system is broken and now so full of fake and even fraudulent reviews it has lost all meaning. Basic tricks like aggregating reviews for several products or even switching reviews over to a completely different product are common and no attempt seems to be made to stop this practice.3. Prime Delivery - This increased significantly in price and whereas once next day delivery was the norm, the minimum I am now quoted is 3 to 5 days with most items not even despatching for a couple of days after the order - as bad as the free delivery for non-prime members. It is not unusual for items to take two to three weeks to arrive despite paying the Prime premium.I am also seeing a lot of instances where the item goes to "collected by courier" status very quickly preventing order cancellation but no further movement or valid training information appears for several days suggesting that the item has probably not actually been despatched and that status change was just to stop me cancelling when I discover the delay.4. Prime Video - This was always a bit of a rip-off with most items incurring an extra charge on top of prime membership but the latest change forces you to pay an extra subscription on top of the already expensive Prime membership to get the add free viewing I got for free up until now.5. Prime music - this is another service that has been deliberately made almost unusable unless you want to pay yet another addition subscription on top.6. Customer services - All contact is via chat or phone, not email, so hard to make formal complaints or keep a paper trail. Although occasionally helpful, most of the time they merely read information to you that you can already see on the website and promises of action are rarely followed through.I have, at one point or another raised all of these issues with Amazon customer services only to be met with responses that ranged from complete indifference to promises to pass on my concerns which clearly went no further because nothing changed.In short, other than the convenience of having so many items in one place there is little to commend this company any more. Amazon Prime in particular is most definitely no longer worth the money.

Review Text: I ordered an IPad Air from Amazon (the company itself rather than a Marketplace seller) on 24th November. I have been posting book reviews on Amazon for many years, always buying the books at the site to get the cachet of “Verified purchase”. My efforts resulted in more than thirty reviews appearing on Amazon, many rated as either “Top Positive Review” or “Top Critical Review”. But when I submitted a review of “The Last Politician” by Franklin Foer, I got a terse email from Amazon that it could not be posted “because it doesn’t meet our guidelines for one or more of these reasons: Profanity, Harassment, Hate Speech, Sexual Content, Illegal Activity, Private Information”. This had never happened before, and I was quite surprised. I went to the link that showed the “Community Guidelines” and read all six pages, scratching my head, trying to figure what I’d done wrong and then I realized the issue was politics. The person checking my review was apparently an extreme liberal so I made some changes that I thought might let my piece “pass” and I resubmitted it. But I soon realized this was a waste of time because I could make changes piecemeal again and again, but without knowing exactly what in my 850 word review was the ”problem”, my efforts would be fruitless.How could I get the nameless and faceless Amazon person behind the “wizard’s curtain” to tell me what to do? I remembered seeing on my “Author’s Page” a place where I could recommend books. I’d never used this feature before but now got the idea to cite Franklin Foer’s book as a “Recommendation”, writing in the comments, “I wrote a review of this book that did not pass the Amazon Moderator and I hope they will tell me what to change.” This was an act of desperation because I truly wanted to get my review posted and I was willing to make rewrites but had to have some guidance, sort of like we got from our high school English teacher who would take a red pencil and underline the problem.Apparently, my ploy with Amazon backfired because I soon got an email saying my post was “outside of our guidelines” and “consider this to be a first warning.” Amazon’s ire was about the book recommendation I’d put on my author’s page (specifically the comments showing Amazon in a bad light) since this was the only “post” I’d ever made other than book reviews.This was going nowhere, and I was not going to play Amazon’s games. I replied to the email, saying, “if you cannot tell me what I am doing wrong I will cancel my book advertising, Amazon Prime, and the Amazon prime credit card and quit making purchases from Amazon.” Six days later I got a reply email saying, “You have repeatedly posted content that violates our Community Guidelines . . . [and therefore] we’ve removed your ability to participate in Community features.” This was untrue because I’d only made one post, the one where I said, “I hope they [Amazon Moderator] will tell me what to change [in the review that had been rejected].”Unfortunately, all the book reviews I’d posted on Amazon over the years were deleted. This was quite disappointing because I’d spent hundreds of dollars on dozens of books, reading them closely over countless hours in order to write honest and informed book reviews and now my work had come to naught. I truly doubt that anyone has put more effort(both in the reading and the writing) into creating a book review than I have. Amazon’s actions have not only hurt me but are a disservice to millions of readers who rely on quality reviews to make wise decisions in their book purchases.As I said earlier, I’ve submitted critical assessments of other books to Amazon and never had a problem and I must conclude the current issue is over politics, simply having a different opinion. While I did say some positives about the author, I also faulted him for being almost sycophantic toward Biden. What he wrote was an uncritical fluff piece and I called it as such. The review, as written, would be passable to any reasonable person and there is nothing out of bounds in it. I read the book thoroughly and wrote an honest, critical review with no malice or evil intent. For anyone interested, a google search of “book reviews of ‘The Last Politician’” will take you to Goodreads where you’ll find my piece and you can decide for yourself.

Dissatisfied with Amazon's Recent Policies and ServiceI have been a loyal Amazon customer for many years, but recent experiences have left me deeply dissatisfied with the company's policies and service. I want to emphasize that my dissatisfaction is not directed at any specific representative but is primarily related to systemic issues stemming from Amazon's new policies.​ Incorrect Items Received: On multiple occasions, I have received the wrong items in my orders. These mistakes not only caused inconvenience but also resulted in wasted time and resources as I had to arrange returns and replacements.​ Items Not Received and Police Report: One incident stands out where a package mysteriously disappeared. I had to file a police report due to the significant value of the missing items. This was an extremely distressing experience and raises concerns about Amazon's delivery and security measures.​ Items Delivered to the Wrong Address: I have also faced situations where items were marked as "delivered" but were, in reality, delivered to the wrong address. This forced me to engage in a time-consuming process to track down and retrieve my packages.​ Refund Delays: The most frustrating aspect of my recent interactions with Amazon has been the extensive delays in processing refunds. Waiting for 30 to 60 days for a refund is not just an inconvenience but also feels like a tactic akin to withholding customer funds.​ This pattern of behavior resembles actions taken by financial institutions to retain customers' money rather than providing satisfactory customer service. It is disheartening to witness Amazon, a company I once held in high regard, resorting to such practices.​ As a result of these recurring issues and my growing frustration, I have made the difficult decision to discontinue my patronage of Amazon. While I have enjoyed the convenience and variety of products offered in the past, the recent decline in service quality and the apparent disregard for customer satisfaction have left me with no choice.​ I hope that by sharing my experiences, Amazon will take the necessary steps to address these issues and improve its customer service. It is my belief that companies should prioritize customer satisfaction over all else, as loyal customers are the lifeblood of any business.​ In conclusion, I can no longer place my trust in Amazon as a reliable online shopping platform, and I will be seeking alternatives for my future purchases.

In recent times, there have been numerous instances of account closures by e-commerce giant Amazon without any explanation or proper communication to the affected customers. These abrupt closures have left customers frustrated, confused, and feeling violated. A negative trend of unexplained account closures is observed, highlighting the negative impact on customers and questioning the ethical practices of a company that prides itself on customer-centricity. Many customers, like myself, have fallen victim to Amazon's sudden account closures. Without warning or prior notice, access to accounts that have been faithfully used for years is abruptly terminated. When attempting to log in, a message appears stating that the account has been closed, with an email notification supposedly sent. However, in numerous cases, customers claim to have never received any such email or any details on how to resolve the situation.Adding to the frustration, attempts to seek clarification from Amazon's customer support often go unanswered. It is only when customers create new accounts and reach out to support that they receive a response, albeit in a rude form. The response typically states that the account was closed for violating the terms of the Conditions of Use agreement. However, customers vehemently deny any wrongdoing and are left perplexed by the lack of specific reasons for their account closures.Account closures without proper explanation or justification raise severe concerns about customer rights. As loyal patrons who have spent years and significant amounts of money on the platform, customers have the right to transparency and fair treatment. The sudden termination of access to accounts, which may contain valuable digital assets such as e-books and audio files, feels like a betrayal of trust. The alarming trend of unexplained account closures by Amazon raises serious questions about the company's commitment to customer satisfaction and respect for customer rights.

There's plenty to like about Amazon when it works. They sell more or less everything, and lots of it can be with you by tomorrow. But, for a company that is declaring profits bigger than some national budgets, they could shave just a little off that to provide actual customer service, for those occasions when it doesn't simply go right. There simply is no way to get hold of them. If you try to begin a complaint, or ask a question, the site will guide you through a million useless questions, in the assumption that you can only have a problem that they have foreseen, and that you can be guided to an automated procedure. If you really persist, this experience will become circular, as you glimpse buttons that you think will help, but actually take you back to an earlier point in the process. Eventually, you may spot the very well hidden 'contact us' button that appears if you go round three times, and insist each time that your problem isn't listed. Sadly this contact is a chat that is -without wanting to offend those who man cheap call centres - far less intelligent than a bot. Today I had the issue that a number of Kindle books have gone from my library. When you're removing them from a device, one button says, "remove download" whilst another says, "delete," and the latter actually removes the book clean out of your library on the Amazon server. No idea why this would even be a possiblity, let alone so easy to do, but someone in our family managed to wipe a massive chunk of our library whilst emptying a Kindle. It took me about 10 attempts to explain to the guy on the other end that this is even possible - after each attempt he sent me a link to my library, insisting that the books must be there if I bought them. Eventually he pretended the chat had been quiet for too long (5 seconds) and passed it off to someone whose English and knowledge of Amazon was even worse. After reviewing the whole thing again with him, and receiving the same patronisation, he assured me there was nothing that can be done. I told him this isn't correct because I know people who have done it, by virtue of getting a slightly better assistant. Then I provided him with the order number for one of the books that is missing, so he could see that there is still a receipt in my order history, but that the book no longer appears in my library. At this point he told me that Amazon only archive invoices for a year or so, so he wouldn't be able to see a record of the order. I explained that I was looking at the record of the order, by logging into my Amazon account, which resides on their servers, so this was clearly a lie. At that point he simply closed the chat window. Normally I wouldn't go to the trouble of venting somewhere about this, but it's now about the tenth such experience I've had. This one is arguably partly my fault (although there's really no reason to have an option to completely remove books from your library, and certainly not to make it so easily done), but usually it's a complete screw up on their part, and you're still dealing with someone who can just hang up if they don't feel like helping.

I am writing this review to express my deep disappointment with Amazon's delivery service, which has proven to be increasingly terrible and far from cost-effective. It is truly baffling how one can place an order for a product, only to have it delivered at the very last minute. As a Prime subscriber, I had high expectations when I placed an order for a printer in the afternoon of the day before, expecting a smooth and timely delivery process. However, my experience quickly turned into a frustrating ordeal.The delivery time for my order was changed multiple times, causing significant inconvenience. It went from an initial estimated time of noon to an ever-shifting schedule that ultimately settled on 7.15 PM the next day. Throughout the entire process, I had to wait anxiously, as the delivery time continued to be revised. It is truly disheartening to witness such a lackluster level of service from a company that prides itself on efficiency. The entire day was put on hold as I eagerly awaited the arrival of my order.What makes matters worse is the fact that the delivery time extended all the way until 10 PM, and yet, I am still here waiting. This constant rescheduling and prolonged waiting period have only added to my frustration and dissatisfaction. It has become evident that the convenience I expected from Amazon's Prime service is simply not worth the trouble.I can't help but compare this experience to that of a third-world service, as the level of inefficiency and unreliability is truly reminiscent of subpar delivery systems. It is worth mentioning that since Amazon's unionization, the quality of service seems to have taken a noticeable downturn. While I understand that various factors can contribute to delivery delays, the continuous changes and lack of punctuality are simply unacceptable.I hope this review sheds light on my disappointing experience and highlights the urgent need for improvement in Amazon's delivery service. I trust that Amazon will take these concerns seriously and strive to regain the trust of its customers by delivering on its promises of timely and efficient service.

An Honest Review of Amazon I have been an Amazon customer for several years now, and I believe it's time to share an honest review of my experiences with the e-commerce giant. While Amazon offers numerous advantages and convenience, it also has its fair share of drawbacks that need to be acknowledged. Here's my breakdown of the pros and cons:Pros:1. Vast Product Selection: One of Amazon's biggest strengths is its unparalleled product range. From electronics to clothing, home goods to books, you can find almost anything you need on their platform.2. Competitive Prices: Amazon's marketplace fosters competition among sellers, often resulting in competitive prices. You can often find great deals and discounts on various products.3. Convenience and Speed: Amazon's Prime membership offers fast and free shipping on eligible items, making it incredibly convenient for time-sensitive purchases. Additionally, their user-friendly interface and seamless checkout process enhance the overall shopping experience.4. Customer Reviews: The abundance of customer reviews provides valuable insights and helps make informed purchasing decisions. It's beneficial to hear others' experiences before making a purchase.Cons:1. Counterfeit Products: Due to the sheer number of sellers on Amazon, there is a risk of encountering counterfeit or low-quality items. While Amazon takes measures to combat this issue, it remains a concern for some buyers.2. Third-Party Seller Discrepancies: As Amazon allows third-party sellers, inconsistencies in product quality, customer service, and shipping practices can occur. It's essential to research sellers and read reviews before making a purchase.3. Environmental Impact: The rapid growth of Amazon's operations has raised concerns about its environmental impact, such as packaging waste and carbon emissions from delivery vehicles. They have made some efforts to address these concerns, but there is still room for improvement.4. Worker Conditions: Over the years, there have been reports and controversies regarding the working conditions at Amazon's fulfillment centers. These issues highlight the need for better worker treatment and labor practices.Overall, Amazon remains a convenient and popular platform for online shopping, but it's important to approach it with awareness of its limitations. Being an informed shopper and understanding the potential drawbacks can help mitigate any negative experiences. Amazon's continuous improvements and addressing of these concerns would undoubtedly contribute to a better customer experience and make it an even more reliable platform in the future.

Review Title: Does not reliably deliver on delivery promises, questionable products from big name brands
Review Text: This review is based upon a continued worsening of service from Amazon. We have been doing business with Amazon since late 2016, and had mostly satisfactory service from them until the pandemic happened. Our biggest problem is a failure to deliver products on time, if at all. For example. I was just informed for the 4th time in a single week that an order was going to be late, or as with the one I was just informed of, completely undeliverable. This used to happen on occasion, but now happens regularly. Dealing with customer service is just some customer service rep repeating a sentence, phrase or paragraph from the "how to get rid of (choose your own descriptor) customer as quickly as possible with as little help/work as possible" book they must all be handed the second they are hired. The second problem we regularly deal with, from day one, is receiving faulty, fake, knock-off, etc. products from "big brand" names, such as Energizer (entire 12-pack of CR2450 batteries that were bad), Wrangler (jeans that look like factory rejects, buttons sewed in wrong spot, horrible dye jobs), so on and so forth. That problem was easily solved, only order the cheap knock-off items from Amazon, that way you know what to expect. We order the name brand stuff from Walmart, and those orders rarely arrive late and/or in bad condition.We have tried to be understanding of the problems going on in the world, but we pay for the prime membership mainly for the free two-day shipping promises, and Amazon just cannot deliver on that any longer. Also, if they are able to pull my money immeditately upon "placing order", then I shouldn't have to wait 5 business days for a return of my $71 for an order that became "undeliverable" on the day it was supposed to be delivered. We cancelled the membership today, and decided to leave a review here, not necessarily to try to hurt Amazon, but to make future customers aware of problems they will likely run into.

Review Title: I've been an Amazon Prime member for a…
Review Text: I've been an Amazon Prime member for a long time.  And in all that time, I've witnessed and experienced a progressive erosion in the quality of service provided by, and an increased lack of professionaIism, diligence, understanding, and/or intelligence on the part of Amazon's Customer Service staff.  Today was the worst, most nightmarish experience yet.  I had to return a malfunctioning Fire TV.  Everything went smoothly until I received the replacement TV today.  It arrived without a remote, power cord, or legs. Now whether or not I was supposed to KEEP those parts from the TV I returned, I have no idea.  None of the reps I dealt with at the time said anything of the sort.   So I spent over 3 hours on the phone or chat with Amazon trying to figure out the easiest way to get a TV that was complete and works.  I was transferred to various individuals (11 at last count -- and I was disconnected or cut off from THREE of those) all saying they would fix the problem to my satisfaction.  However, nothing ever ever happened and the only solution that they could ultimately come up with is for me to return THIS TV as well, and they'd issue a refund (when they're good and ready). Some of the suggestions provided by some of the agents were frankly ludicrous.  One actually suggested that I go online (on Amazon, of course) and order the missing parts, purchase them, and then request a REFUND for those items FROM Amazon! When I asked if she could provide me those item numbers (since she was supposedly affiliated with their "special" Fire TV unit), or better yet JUST SEND ME those missing parts, she simply ignored my request.  Especially when I asked why she thought it would be acceptable for me to PAY again for something that should have been included WITH the TV to begin.Anyway, towards the end of all of this, having hit the end of my patience, the reps wouldn't even listen to me, went into some spiel about how they are entitled to terminate their calls, which several of them did.  The follow-up emails I received were just as abrupt and helpless/hopeless.  So I'm sitting here with a TV that is no use to me; waiting for UPS to pick it up to return it.  And then -- once Amazon in Lexington KY gets it -- I'll have to wait a good month or longer to see a penny of what I've paid.  Frankly, I'm not holding my breath. One also says they DO have a bit of autonomy and flexibility regarding what they can and cannot do for a customer.  Again, color me doubtful:  all I was told over and over again today (from 95% of those I spoke to or dealt with) is essentially their hands are tied, and they are limited to what they can or cannot do based on their systems and its policies.

Review Title: Amazon Delivery doesn't really know how to deliver anything
Review Text: I have been a loyal amazon prime customer for years. I ordered an XTERRA 4500 Treadmill on January 9th, 2023 and paid the additional $99 for assembly and room of choice delivery. On January 13th, a third party delivery service "JB Hunt" Arrived at my door, and the delivery drivers informed me that the treadmill was too heavy to take upstairs, and offered to leave it in the garage. I informed them that I had paid for the room of choice service, and they said to contact Amazon to establish different delivery options. I called Amazon that day, spending more than 3 hours on the phone being transferred between multiple departments from account services, to heavy and bulky, to home services. During that phone call, the customer service representative in Heavy and Bulky assured me that Jb Hunt had no right to refuse delivery because I had paid for room of choice, and the treadmill only weighed 213 lbs. He assured me that if I reschedule the delivery, they will redeliver it, and that he could not change the delivery company. Consequently, I rescheduled the delivery for Wednesday, January 18th. On that day,  The same Jb Hunt driver arrived and informed me that they could not take the treadmill up the stairs. I contacted Amazon for a second time and Amazon apologized profusely and provided me a 20% discount for my inconvenience issued as a gift card, And reassured me again that Jb Hunt should have delivered the package, and rescheduled a 3rd re delivery attempt for the following day. On January 19th, Jb Hunt did not even bother to show up. Instead, the order was cancelled, unilaterally and marked fraudulently by Jb Hunt and marked as undeliverable for lack of access to the front door, which is NOT true. I called Amazon, and they informed me that I could fill out a special form with their heavy and bulky department that would specify that I do not wish Jb Hunt to deliver products to me anymore, and to re-order the treadmill. After filling out that form, and attempting to re-order the treadmill, I found that Amazon refused to give me the 20% discount on the 2nd order for my inconvenience. Honestly, after 9 hours of waiting through their delivery windows, and spending more than 6 hours on the phone with Amazon customer service to figure out how this Treadmill should get this delivered, I found it shocking that Amazon refused to carry the 20% discount to my 2nd attempt at purchasing the treadmill, even though I would have been able to get that 20% if Jb Hunt would have delivered the package like they were supposed to. In summary, Amazon delivery and logistics is a mess. The left hand does not know what the right hand is doing, and their third party delivery contractors such as Jb Hunt refused to do what they are contractually obligated to do and the customer is caught in the middle. Amazon kept insisting that Jb Hunt must deliver, and Jb Hunt refused to deliver and I wasted more than 15 hours of my life trying to coordinate between the two. I cancelled my prime membership because honestly, prime delivery is more like crappy delivery.

Review Title: A true story about Stephane and Menzzo
Review Text: A true story about Stephane and Menzzo, a company  supported by Amazon. Ripping of people can have heartbreaking consequencesSummer 2020, after 15 years of marriage, my friend Stephane and his wife are separating. Life stops for Stéphane for a moment, he rents a small apartment in Brussels, except for a chair and a table, there is nothing there, the once so lively creative man was onlya shadow of himself. He misses his two daughters very much during the week. After a hopeless year, of intense sadness, in 2021, Stéphane decides to put his life back on track, he works very hard, as a freelance cameraman, also for our company, and takes care of his 2 children with great pleasure and dedication during the weekend. He saves as much money as possible, lives like a hermit and is convinced to lead a respectable life again in no time. After a few months of saving, Stéphane decides to place an order at a French low budget, online furniture store, to finally furnish his apartment, fully motivated he really wanted to make a new start. Unfortunately something goes wrong with the delivery. (what we don't know and is also irrelevant) The goods go back to the supplier and Stéphane waits months to see his money back. Unfortunately after dozens of apologies, the money is not coming back. He no longer has any savings and at his small apartment in Brussels, the social inspector comes by one day after a complaint from his ex-wife, where according to her the children did not have the necessary accommodation to stay with daddy. After this visit we never heard from our friend again, he used his only furniture, his table and chair to do the most unthinkable and took his own life. Months after his death we found printed advertising in his drawer, from a few furniture companies, also Menzzo, we read some reviews and together with the editors decided to place an order at both companies, we ordered a table at one company, with a value of 700 €, this was returned and within a week we had all our money back. On the same day, we ordered 12 chairs from Menzzo, for a value of € 1250, until the end of last week, we did everything we could to get our money back , hoping that our suspicion would not be correct, but unfortunately we also keep getting to hear another excuse and another and another ....so we realize our money will never be paid back again. Our intention is certainly not to shame a company, we ourselves realize how difficult doing business is and that comments are always relative. That is why we decided to do the test ourselves, despite the many negative reviews already suggesting that the same pattern could be observed here as told by our good friend at the time. It is therefore only a suspicion that our friend ordered from them, yet they use the same method to rob people in this way and we found the printed adds remember. The customers who order furniture from Menzzo and other rogue companies are usually guided (misled) by cheap prices and are therefore happy that they can also afford a new table, chair or sofa, often they have to make a huge financial shortfall for this and use their last pennies to realize a small dream to have a dignified life again. Often it turns out that this trust is only a one-way street, deceit, abuse of trust and the umpteenth blow, which can lead to even the most ultimate act for people like Stéphane. Fortunately, there are still many companies that mean well. We can only hope that with the introduction of our website, good people like Stéphane will be warned about companies such as Menzzo. and their collaborators, because one day on Judgment Day, whatever your faith is, you will be welcomed by someone like Stéphane, or maybe by your own grandmother, grandfather, mother, father.... deeply disappointed in the choices you've made, ripping of other people, by the sad disillusioned look in their eyes, you can see, you did the wrong thing, no matter how hard you are trying to ignore it , carma can never be avoided. Not here, not now, not later.Please make sure that kind people like Stéphane, can't be the victim anymore of lawless CEO's like D.M. and all of his co-workers. Everyone of them is guilty, because they just have other choices. Don't buy from them, they are not worth it, inform Amazon of their practices, Facebook and other social media, the only way you can hurt them, is to hurt them in their wallet, because a heart they don't have.

Review Title: No Item Arrived. Company Lied About Refund Processing.
Review Text: I have been an Amazon customer for the better part of two decades, most of that time being a subscriber to their Prime service. Up until now I have always had satisfactory service when and if having to deal with customer care. I ordered an upholstered queen size headboard on December 10th, 2022, which was supposed to arrive by UPS on December 19th. On the 19th I was given notice that an item had arrived at my residence. When I arrived home, there was no such item. I contacted customer care a total of four times that evening and was told numerous things. First, I was told that “carriers will mark an item down as delivered even if the item has not arrived yet.” I found that to be a very misleading statement to make, and one that does not fall under the realm of professional business practice. If an item has not yet arrived, why on earth would it be marked down as delivered? I was then asked to wait 24 hours until the following day, Tuesday December 20th 7pm EST specifically, because sometimes items arrive late. I was told that if it hadn’t arrived by that time, that a refund would be issued to me. On Tuesday December 20th I re-contacted customer care three more times in an attempt to let them know that I STILL had not received my paid for item. I was not given a refund as had been stated to me the previous day, instead I was told simply to “file a police report”. In addition to filing that report, I also filed a report with the Better Business Bureau for the completely shady way that this situation was handled, and the run-around that I was given. It is now Thursday, December 22nd and I am still without the item that I had paid for, as well as out of the money used to purchase the item. I have discontinued my Amazon Prime membership and will not be shopping through this company any longer.

Thank you Amazon! I think people take for granted orders and deliveries and how much logistics is involved. Considering how close we are to Christmas and still able to get deliveries for next day and returns are so easy and no quibble. Thanks to all the staff at Amazon and hope you all enjoy your festive season too!

Review Title: Amazon charging policies and bad customer service "Marie Dee"
Review Text: I personally don't keep a lot of funds in my checking account unless I am planning on making a card purchase, and when I do need to make a purchase, I transfer enough to my checking to make the purchase. This has been frustrating for me because I'll place an order, not be charged for days, then get an email that the order is delayed for card declining, then rerun the card, wait MORE days and have more delays just for the issue to repeat itself. It literally says in the chat transcript that she left the chat. I didn't curse, I didn't attack her or even the company, I was just pursuing an answer for what I thought was a pretty straightforward question and I guess she was frustrated that I wasn't accepting the canned macro script she was feeding me.I'm leaving a 2 star instead of 1 because I started up another chat immediately after with "Himanshu", who was kind and actually offered me a workaround. I can't change the charging time (time of order vs. time of shipping process beginning) if I use my debit card, BUT if I put the needed balance for the order on an Amazon gift card instead and use that for the purchase, I can avoid all the previous issues I've had and not worry about maintaining my checking balance for a charge that could come at any time.

Review Title: This review is for one employee at…
Review Text: This review is for one employee at Amazon in particular - Shy Lauri.Before I begin, I just want it to be known that although I am now hoping to get a job at Amazon, I had no personal affiliation with Amazon or it's employees (including Shy Lauri) during the time period for which I am writing this review:I am homeless. Something has changed at Amazon. I went to post the following review for Zipp Battery YTX30L-BS Maintenance Free Replacement Battery for ATV.  Amazon, decided to censor my review and refused to post it.  They say people only want to know about the product, and not the entire process...bull sh**.  I want to know the entire experience and I am sure you would too. Amazon says..."What's not allowed:Seller, order, or shipping feedbackWe don't allow reviews or questions and answers that focus on:Sellers and the customer service they provideOrdering issues and returnsShipping packagingProduct condition and damageShipping cost and speedWhy not? Community content is meant to help customers learn about the product itself, not someone's individual experience ordering it." I have found that everything boils down to money or power.  In this case, I believe, it was money.They never shipped this battery in a protective shipping box.  They shipped it only in its display box.  Mind you, this battery has a lot of metal (lead) in it and its very heavy.  Everything from Amazon that I have ever received, always comes in its own padded protective shipping medium.  None of this damage would have happened if this battery was shipped correctly.   This battery was left flopping around inside its box with virtually no protection.   I have the pictures and have them available.  The battery then sat on my counter top for a few weeks.  I then noticed it had leaked a pool of acid off to its right.  Unbeknownst to me, I now can see that this battery had internal damage, root cause unknown.  I then promptly cleaned up the acid using water and a small amount of baking soda to neutralize the acid.  At this point I was hoping that everything would be ok.  I came back a few days later to find the counter top had sustained permanent damage.  We will now have to replace a counter top costing hundreds of dollars.  Looking back, I believe this was the following scenario...Company has a bad battery.   Company wants to maximize profits so company sends out defective battery in its display packaging as company knows it is not adequate to protect battery, thus battery and display box will be damaged enough to blame the shipper and company can then file a claim and make its money.  Meanwhile, customer gets taken advantage of as he/she is told they do not have to send it back but now might have to pay hazardous waste fees to dispose of it and may even sustain other expenses (in my case, a new counter top).  The Shipper is out money...the Customer is out money...and the Company wins $$$!  Again, this would have never happened if the battery was shipped in a protective padded shipping box. Amazon has already seen this review prior to them refusing to list it.  As of now, they have not reached out to right their wrong.

Review Text: I received the wrong item from an Amazon purchase and returned it.  The total cost of the item was approx. $500. To add insult to injury purchases were posted against the gift card vs my Amazon credit card so they won’t refund the remaining gift card balance to my Amazon credit card!!  This seems to be entrapment, as Amazon’s messaging regarding where the funds are being returned to isn’t clear!  It seems Amazon is intentionally using vague language in their auto pre-selected option for returned funds to ensure customers spend the returned money through their company!  If this is unintentional, Amazon should add “gift card” to the auto pre-selected return funds option so customers understand the funds will not be returned to their Amazon credit card used to make the purchase, but instead be added to a non-existent gift card balance.  The gift card was created at the time of the refund!  As I stated above, this seems like financial entrapment to ensure returned funds remain with AMAZON vs being credited to the Amazon credit card used to make the purchase! I believe any reasonable person would assume “be returned to Amazon account balance” means being returned to your Amazon credit card balance.  Especially since at the time of the return there were no other Amazon account balances other than the credit card, there weren’t any gift cards on file, and every other refund processed through Amazon had been credited to my Amazon credit card balance. When “gift card” isn’t in the sentence of the pre-selected option, and Amazon has credit card options, it seems like it is an intentional action by Amazon to be vague in their messaging to entrap customer’s funds and ensure more funds are expended through Amazon!  I rarely write reviews, but felt people should know about Amazon’s ridiculous refund policy/messaging, as it could really cause harm to families already in financial distress due to the resent pandemic and resulting economic downturn.

Review Title: Great pricing, lack of transparency and accountability
Review Text: While Amazon's prices are normally way better than other companies selling the same thing their delivery system is flawed endlessly. They promise 1-day or 2-day deliveries and 7 out of 10 times they are never delivered in the promised time frame. What they do not tell you is that they have a clause that is not clearly posted anywhere for you to easily say. It says that the delivery time begins when the item is actually shipped. So, if you order an item on a Saturday and it says it will be delivered on Monday by 10 p.m. this estimate will only be accurate if the item was picked up by the carrier on Saturday. Now shipping delays happen and often they do happen as a result of the carrier so that is completely out of Amazon's hands but change the system to more accurately reflect these delays.Quit making promises that you knowingly cannot keep. Additionally, if an item is not able to be delivered because it is damaged in the transit process then include that reason in the email when you cancel the order. This actually just happened to me. In fact, it is the second time in a month that I ordered an item that I never got.Previously I ordered an item that the third-party vendor said was in stock but were unable to fulfill the order because they banked on the parts being in stock when they were going to be shipped. This didn't happen and they simply refunded my money with no explanation as to why.In both cases I had to call the vendor and Amazon to get details on why. Amazon needs to hold themselves and their vendors accountable for the accuracy of their descriptions. From shipping lead times to availability of items.While ordering online is convenient and often times less expensive it is beginning to show the weaknesses that are apparent. At least when you go to a brick-and-mortar store you know whether they have the item and if not, you move on to find it elsewhere.  There is no expectation that you are being told it is in stock when it really isn't. Their inventory is what it is. We are using online services such as Amazon with the expectation that they are going to be upfront with regards to inventory levels and shipping estimates. Not to be told that there are 15 items in stock, or it is a 2-day delivery and then not be able to fulfill these promises more often than not. Quit trying to look spectacular only to look lackluster most of the time. Prices are not everything when you cannot get the items anyways. I gave Amazon 2 stars only because of pricing. However, if the issues continue my 15-year history with them is gone. I will gladly pay more and be part of their solution to the problem by seeing them go the way of K-Mart and Sears.

I have a love/hate relationship with Amazon. I order from them all the time, especially the last few years because it is easier than having to go out and search our local stores for particular items, that often times are not in stock or simply not available where I live. I have also often searched for other online stores to purchase items from but rarely do I find one where I can get free shipping and a lower price. So, though it pains me to do so, if I need to place an order for certain items, I shop on Amazon. That being said, the customer service I personally have received has been pretty awesome, the majority of the time. The key is NOT to buy from a third party seller, as that is a huge headache, in my own experience. Also, you cannot write a review that directly complains about Amazon because they will not "approve" it. Which is ridiculous because we all know that Amazon has gone way downhill since the early days. However, that being said, it is possible to get a refund, make a return, and get your money back if you NEVER receive your package. It is a bit of a pain in the a** but it can be done be done. What it takes is patience, persistence, and knowing how to navigate the system. Sometimes it takes more than one phone call and asking for a supervisor, explaining the situation over and over again, but in the end the result is in my favor. I actually fill out the survey the customer service agents email me after the phone call. I am honest and thorough when I fill them out and I praise those exceptional agents who go the extra mile for me, as I appreciate excellent service, as I have been in there shoes in the past. However, if I can find an alternative to shopping at Amazon that also offers free shipping and lower prices, I take it. I would love nothing more than to not have to order another item from them. Obviously, the company treats their employees like crap, the quality of many of their products is merde, they often price gouge, many of their reviews are bogus, the packages are usually not packaged properly or poorly packaged, returns have become a huge pain, many third party sellers rip people off, it can take longer to receive refunds and reviews have to be approved(utter.bullsh**.) Jeff Bezos is making money hand over first, while not paying the amount of taxes or any at all on the billions of dollars he has made and not caring one iota about his employees or his customers. This is what happens when we end up with monopolies and extremely few options available to us. My goal this year is to buy less, continue to search for other online businesses to shop from (especially local ones) and continue to vote, sign petitions and work towards changing the current status quo.

I asked her if they could leave something that would let the Amazon shipping center in Virginia (where it was headed) that when they got the package it should be returned to me. She said that Amazon had no such system and I would need to wait until the [package made it to the facility. I asked her if she could put me through to the facility in Virginia so I could tell them myself. She said she had no such ability. I asked if she could transfer me to someone who could contact them. She explained that there was no such person. I thanked her for her time and called UPS again. This time, UPS said they would issue an interception order to stop the package from arriving. Frustrated, I called Amazon again and spoke to someone about the issue. I explained the situation and asked if she could get the package sent back to me. She explained that she was sorry, but the person who spoke to me last gave me false information. There was, in fact, a system of tickets that could be created to notify a shipping facility of a package that should be returned to the sender upon arrival. She told me that since the package arrived at the facility that morning, it has likely been opened, inspected, and the contents thrown away without me being notified. I explained to her that this was a departure from what the other representative told me and that the pictures on the film were for a music festival and were irreplaceable She apologized and said she would file a ticket anyway, just in case, but that I should expect to not get my pictures back. She sighed and stated that things "could have been very different" if the first Amazon representative gave me the correct information. I asked why the system takes 15 days when packages are delivered sometimes in less than 2 days. She did not have an answer to this question. Frustrated, I explained that what was originally a mixup due to my lapse of memory has become the imminent loss of irreplaceable photo work and film rolls which were valued at a combined $45. I asked who I should speak to to get compensation for this incident in the event that I never get my film rolls back. Amazon DecrepitudeI had trouble deciding whether to choose one or two stars for my review.In the past you could count on Amazon customer reviews to help you sort out whether a particular item was any good or not. Reviews would tell you about user experiences; how well the product worked, whether there were warranty claim issues, whether the item was suitable for a task, or even if a particular  vendor was untrustworthy or not.However, Amazon started adding Ratings which are not Reviews, simply some useless, lazy person simply giving stars (1-5) without any reason for the rating. Some products have tons of ratings without a single useful note giving a reason for the rating. This is especially infuriating when it comes to reviewing books. You click on what you think is a review and it turns out to be a rating, meaning there is no reason given for the star assignment. This is not very helpful to help you decide if you would be interested in purchasing a book.Later on Amazon removed all of the Comments that customers used to give additional information or commentary on a particular Review. This meant that warning about certain vendors failure to ship products on time, substituting products, shipping used items that were supposed to be new, or explaining why the negative review was a user caused, rather than a product problem.Removing the Comments on Reviews means that a TON OF HELPFUL information is gone resulting in the customer REVIEWS, are no longer as informative and helpful.Of course the worse thing that Amazon had done starting at least 10 years ago is that they lump reviews of different products together, presumably to make it appear that there are more reviews than actually exist. Whenever you purchase an product, you are invited, and encourage to leave a review, which is tied to the purchase of the exact item you purchased so there is no reasonable excuse for claiming that it is hard to connect the review to the exact item purchased. Amazon has all of the data that is needed to do this right.One terrible example of product Review LUMPING are those for Computer Hard Drives (HDs). Amazon lumps the reviews for old generation small capacity 500 Gb HDs, with all hard drives   made by a particular manufacturer with the largest capacity 18TB HDs. Now, the lower capacity HDs were designed and manufactured many years ago, using very different designs and components than those  newest, ultra high capacity HDs. These newest HD's that are very different from the older HDs, and use components that were produced most recently. We know that batches of components of the same design made at different times in factories may have quality control issues, hence Amazon's LUMPING practice defies reason and is DISHONEST.  Amazon will no doubt claim that their filtering menu takes care of this issue, but in fact that is false. You cannot evaluate the percentage of negative reviews (such as adding the two lowest star ratings together) without having these required data easily available. These are not easily found without counting every review. I certainly do not have time to do that, nor should that be required of anyone wanting to understand the review ratings. This would not be a problem if products that are not identical were not LUMPED together.LUMPING is misleading, and seriously dishonest, making it extremely difficult to make choosing a reliable product from Amazon. This practice should certainly stop, and the Review Comments should be put back if possible, and certainly re-instated.I have complained vigorously with customers support and even tried contacting Amazon upper management without success. Do away with LUMPING and get rid of Ratings instead of having Reviews! What will it take to get Amazon to fix these issues ?

Review Title: I ordered a bottle of dandruff shampoo
Review Text: I ordered a bottle of dandruff shampoo. Around $8.00. and paid with my Mastercard. It came in on time. However, 2 weeks later I received an email from Amazon saying "your package is on its way" huh? Could return it but it was made too complicated the way they wanted me to return it. A square postage paid label was issued and the instructions said to return it by putting the square label on a round bottle.They had sent me a second bottle. I put it away to keep and they just had to bill my card on file.They didn't do that. Instead I got an email from Amazon saying " if you don't pay for the second bottle by (such a date) they would charge me a late fee of $94.00!!!!I didn't want that hanging over my head so I paid for the bottle I never ordered. Around $8.00. No big deal. I received an email from the bank they use to charge credit cards and they confirmed they received my check. I wrote them a check instead of them taking the funds from my credit card.I decided to cancel my credit card but Amazon wouldn't let me. A pop-up came up and said that Amazon requires a credit card so to cancel the card I had to cancel my account.I let it sit as I figured I might buy something later.A couple of weeks after that I received an Amazon credit store card. Only good with Amazon purchases. It was for $600.00! I never asked for this card and if and when I decide to buy something. I didn't know wich card they would bill.When you buy something on credit. You are asked at checkout which card you want them to use.I picked my Mastercard on file. At the same time I deleted the $600.00 card. I did this because Amazon has a reputation of double billing. (Read the reviews). So I immediately locked my Mastercard and had my bank issue a new card with a different number.This at least invalidated my Mastercard and would be denied if someone tried to use it for nefarious reasons.After a few months went by I decided to cancel Amazon completely. Wouldn't you know it had been so long that I had forgotten my password.So I used my email address and pushed the "forgot my password" button. That resulted in my receiving an OTP number.I typed in the OTP number and it took me to a site that had further requirements to make sure it was me. "Okay" I said and I've used 3 different phones over the years.I had to check off my current phone number and nothing happened.My second option was to click on myLG G6 phone. Click? Nothing. I hadn't had the LG 6 for years so that did nothing.My next thing they wanted me to click on my Samsung SE. I haven't had that phone in a long time. I had sold it.That didn't work.The only phone I have now is an iPhone.Wich wasn't listed. So I'm stuck. There's no number to call Amazon to talk to. Even if there was they would not give me my password back. If they even knew what it was.It was a vicious cycle I couldn't break.I tried all the passwords I could think of.Nothing.I was determined and finally I got a page that had the option to "cancel your Amazon account". I had found my old password.I scrolled down to "cancel your account" I clicked on the bar and it asked me why was I canceling my account. I just typed into the "I no longer want an Amazon account"Another page popped up with the option to change my mind or "confirm cancellation"I hit "confirm cancellation". Done!Another page pops up and asked for my username and password. I just closed out of the page.This morning, while checking my email I seen a "you haven't finished closing your account" message from Amazon.I clicked on it and it started the whole process again. I just deleted the email. It didn't really matter because I had changed the card anyway rendering the Mastercard invalid. I counted six Amazon emails. I blocked them out. So for those who are crying that Amazon closed your account. Count your blessings. They did you a favor. But they still keep your credit card. Don't forget to delete it in the app website if you want nothing more to do with Amazon. Too bad, I had a good relationship with them innitialy. Just wanted to say that you can't ask Amazon to close your account in anger because you feel stiffed by them as they will not close it. Some people here are saying "close my account". That means nothing to them. They've been known to charge over and over and renewal accounts will still be charged even know you tell them to stop. You have to do it on your Amazon website. Just follow the complex account closure instructions.I eventually locked my credit card immediately and ask for a new card with a different number. That will render your card invalid and any charges will be denied. Good Luck as they make you jump through hoops to cancel.UPDATE: 12/25/2021 have not been contacted by Amazon for over a year now.
